sources.archival_identifier: Hoover Digital Collections object 331573; OSS Board proceedings, Caserta, 4 May 1944
sources.title: Office of Strategic Services Board Proceedings at OSS Headquarters, Caserta
sources.locator: PDF page 24 of 77, document page 24, paragraph XCIX; the OCR labels the paragraph XCII; lines identifying Sgt. Geno Barbati, Army entry, OSS assignment, duties, and Ford civilian work
sources.rights_notes: A declassified wartime OSS record. Only concise excerpts and project-authored paraphrases are retained; the private Army identifier is not reproduced.

organizations.normalization_notes: Army service is modeled as a military assignment, not civilian employment. Training labels are not converted into unit assignments unless item-level evidence establishes a unit.
Historical sources variously use Ford and Ford Motor Company. No plant, subsidiary, city, or employment dates are inferred unless item-level evidence supplies them.

affiliations.role_title: enlisted soldier before OSS communications assignment
affiliations.date_precision: Month precision from the OSS Board record: Army entry in February 1942 and OSS communications assignment in August 1943; no Army unit or exact transfer day is stated
affiliations.research_notes: The wartime record says Barbati received Air Corps basic training, but it does not establish an Air Corps unit assignment. The index records T/Sgt while the May 1944 board record says Sgt.; the exact private identifier confirms the person despite that rank variation.

affiliations.date_precision: The May 1944 OSS Board record identifies Ford work in civilian life and separately dates Army entry to February 1942; it supplies no employment dates, plant, or city
affiliations.research_notes: Publish as the best-supported last civilian employer before Army service. The source does not say how immediately the Ford job preceded Army entry, so the temporal claim remains high rather than confirmed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Geno Barbati is the Army sergeant described in the May 1944 OSS Board proceedings at Caserta.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Sgt. Geno Barbati ... Entered the Army February 1942
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA index row and wartime OSS proceedings share the exact name and exact private Army identifier; the sources also agree on enlisted Army status.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact uncommon name and exact private Army identifier in two official records. The rank labels T/Sgt and Sgt. differ but are compatible with abbreviation or date variation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The proceedings were created during Barbati's OSS service in May 1944 and provide a dated Army-to-OSS chronology beginning in February 1942.
claims.match_notes: The private identifier was used for identity resolution but is excluded from public citations and downloads. The physical Box 35 file has not been reviewed.

claims.claim_text: Geno Barbati's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the United States Army.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Entered the Army February 1942 ... Assigned to OSS for communications August 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The wartime OSS Board record explicitly dates Barbati's Army entry, Air Corps basic training, and subsequent assignment to OSS communications.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact name and exact private Army identifier shared with the NARA index row.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence from Army entry and training to OSS assignment in August 1943; no narrower Army unit is documented.
claims.match_notes: Model as a military assignment, not civilian employment. Air Corps basic training is not converted into an unsupported unit assignment.

claims.claim_text: Ford Motor Company is the best-supported last civilian employer currently documented for Geno Barbati before Army service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Was press operator and spot welder at Ford Motor Company in civilian life.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The May 1944 OSS Board record identifies Barbati's Ford work and separately dates his Army entry to February 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact name and exact private Army identifier shared with the NARA index row.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as civilian work before wartime service, but the source gives no Ford dates or explicit statement that no other civilian job intervened.
claims.match_notes: No plant, subsidiary, city, start date, or exact end date is inferred. The wording preserves that Ford is the best-supported last civilian employer, not an absolute chronology beyond the accessible evidence.
